findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1601 (and again l.1603): « Since Σ₀ is complete, by Lemma lem:surface_complete lim τ₀ = +∞ » - a missing step, not an error. Lemma lem:surface_complete (ii) (l.781-790) asks the graph Σ over D_R^* to be complete. The completeness of Σ₀ does not give that by itself. The step needs the fact that a finite-length curve of Σ₀ ∩ S with r → 0 cannot converge in M₀ (here GX.E0AxisNoLimit.flat_curve_noLimit, from lem:blunt_spear_neighborhood's chart). The Lean proof supplies that argument directly. It never proves the completeness of the piece (hcomp of trace_tendsto_atTop): the broken line of Lemma 2.8(ii)'s proof is carried into Σ₀ and converges there, which contradicts flat_curve_noLimit.
questions: « Σ₀ is complete » (l.1601): read as the Lipschitz completeness of Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete (CompleteSpace of the induced length space plus continuity of toSubtype into N), OQ-152 (b), the reading CauchySpear takes. The theorem uses only these two fields, not the Cauchy-surface field.

The proof (not the statement) uses OQ-158 reading (a), only through trace_spacelikeDevelopment_openStrip with Ω = openStrip R. The statement does not mention the strip's development, so it reads the same under either answer.

instance: Checked by hand, not as a Lean term (kb/0011: not cheap, because it needs the completeness of an induced length space). N = the flat regular part {r > 0} of E₀ (the instance the T-btz-axis-nolimit audit names for flat_curve_noLimit: W = the regular points of paperInY's image, ψ = the identification), v = 0, R = 1 (R'' = 1/2 for the target's form), τ_S z = 1/‖z‖, Sig = {τ = 1/r}. τ_S is continuous on 0 < ‖z‖. hpos: ‖z‖/2 < 1/‖z‖ iff ‖z‖² < 2, true for ‖z‖ ≤ 1. Graph equivalence: ψ∘paperInY is injective off the axis and rad > 0 on bspear. Metric: minkQ of a developed velocity is −2τ'r' + r'² + r²θ'² (hX of edist_le_seg_unif); on Sig (τ' = −r'/r²) it is (1 + 2/r²) dr² + r² dθ², positive definite, so Sig is a smooth spacelike surface, hence spacelike Lipschitz. Completeness: let ρ' = √(1 + 2/r²). Then ρ → −∞ at 0 (ρ' ≥ √2/r) and ρ → +∞ at ∞ (ρ' ≥ 1), and the induced distance is ≥ |Δρ|. So a Cauchy sequence stays in a compact annulus r₁ ≤ r ≤ r₂, where the length and subspace topologies agree (the metric is uniformly comparable to dr² + dθ²), and it converges. The same comparison gives continuity of toSubtype. Conclusion there: 1/r → +∞, consistent.
kb_proposals: Comparing the induced length of Σ ⊆ N with the pulled length of a parametrisation: Causal.Flat.pathLength_pulled_eq_of_local needs only, at each point, F = k • chartAt(q x)(q ·) near x. For the trace on a blunt spear chart this local fact is GX.E0TraceComplete.trace_chart_local (flatE0_regChart plus graphDev_eq_shift_sectorChartY).

To turn a sequence with summable step lengths into a continuous curve (for curve-based no-limit lemmas such as flat_curve_noLimit), use GX.E0TraceComplete.brokenLine u t = u ⌊t⌋₊ + (t − ⌊t⌋₊)•(u(⌊t⌋₊+1) − u ⌊t⌋₊), continuous on ℝ (continuous_brokenLine), and bound each point by the length of its piece with LocalLengthSpace.edist_le_pathLength. This needs a bound on the path length, not only on edist (pathLength_seg_unif).
